Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Before we move to procurement, our legal team asked for clarification on two narrow items in the order form: 1) confirmation that Lumina retains exclusive ownership of user-submitted prompts and final generated outputs for our productized features, and 2) whether Redwood will be allowed to use accumulated usage/feedback for model training (even in aggregated/derived form).

Appreciate a short call if helpful.

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the clear note. Short answer: we can agree to exclusive ownership of customer-submitted prompts and generated outputs for your productized features, with a couple of guardrails we usually include (runtime use exception for debugging, and telemetry for reliability). That will need an Order Form carveout + a tailored clause in the MSA (we call it the "Output Title & Training Lock" schedule).

I've attached a draft order-form redline (Lumina-OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf) and a 1-page summary of changes. High-level points we propose:
- Customer retains title to prompts and outputs used to power Lumina product features (explicit assignment in the Order Form).
- Redwood may retain pseudonymized telemetry and aggregated usage metrics for operational purposes (SLA, capacity planning) but not use raw prompt-output pairs for model training.
- Mutual-action plan: legal redlines agreed by 9/4, sign by 9/10, pilot go-live week of 9/23.

Looping Laura for legal confirmation on exact language. If your counsel prefers a DocuSign workflow, happy to start it.

Cheers,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quick clarification on Order Form IP carveouts

Elena / team —

Appreciate the flagged items. We reviewed the proposed redline and recommend the following legal-safe compromise to preserve Redwood's ability to operate (and to limit long-term platform entanglement):

1) Output ownership: Order Form will include assignment of title to outputs that are specific to Lumina's configured features. We will add a carveout preserving Redwood's right to use ephemeral runtime state for debugging only (limited retention, access logs).

2) Training and feedback license: Redwood will accept a narrow "non-training" outcome by default: we will not use your raw prompts or outputs to train models. However, we request the right to retain and use aggregated/derived telemetry (no raw text) for safety improvements and kernel-level performance tuning. Where Lumina wants complete training lockbox (zero derived use), we can offer that as a paid enterprise option (Training Lockbox Addendum).

3) Audit and evidence: Lumina asked for proof that data is not used for training. We can commit to a quarterly attestation of data usage in the first year and provide a traceability log for any engineering access to runtime traces (subject to redaction).

4) Recommended language snippets are in the attached PDF. Primary open items: how long runtime traces are retained (we propose 30 days standard, configurable to 7 days for strict customers), and whether aggregated telemetry can include token-level latency histograms (we believe those are fine and operationally important).

Next steps: Marissa, can you confirm Lumina's preference for retention (30 / 14 / 7 days)? Jonas, pls prepare a short exec note if Lumina requests the lockbox add-on (pricing impact).

Laura Bennett
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: training-lockbox-term-sheet.pdf

Elena —

Thanks for working through the language. To keep procurement moving: if Lumina takes the standard 30-day runtime-trace retention and accepts the non-training guarantee (no raw prompt-output pairs used for model training), Redwood will remove the additional "training assignment" line in the MSA and accept the Order Form assignment as the primary path. That avoids broad model-use licenses while keeping SLAs intact.

If Lumina requires absolute lockbox (no derived telemetry), there will be a one-time implementation fee and a modest ARR premium for the operational cost of the lockbox (Jonas will follow up with numbers). Either way, we can prepare a DocuSign packet with the Order Form + Training Lockbox Addendum to capture the selected option.

Proposed mutual action plan (confirmable in DocuSign):
- 9/03: Finalize retention choice & training opt (Lumina)
- 9/06: Redwood issues final Order Form + MSA exhibit
- 9/10: Signatures complete
- 9/23: Pilot provisioned (dedicated tenant)

Marissa: please start the HubSpot deal note and mark legal state as "Awaiting Customer Retention Decision".

Best,
Rishi
